punchline: Sherron Watkins warned Enron's chairman of a wave of accounting scandals, and the review of her memo asked only whether it held new facts.
thirty_sec: Days after Jeffrey Skilling resigned in August 2001, Enron vice president Sherron Watkins wrote to chairman Kenneth Lay that she was nervous the company would implode in a wave of accounting scandals. Lay sent the memo to the law firm Vinson & Elkins, reportedly asking whether it contained new factual information, not for a wider look at the accounts. The firm reported no wrongdoing. Enron filed for bankruptcy on 2 December 2001.
